subject.title: [Feature]: Allow Gateway-relay Talk clients to declare realtime tools

question: Should Gateway-relay Talk support per-session client-declared provider tools, and should the declaration be a public `talk.session.create` input rather than global `talk.realtime` configuration?
rationale: The desired capability crosses the public Gateway protocol, provider bridge, client trust boundary, and configuration surface; source evidence shows the result path exists but does not determine the permanent declaration and authorization contract.

options.title: Approve a session-scoped protocol seam
options.body: Add a typed optional client-tool array to gateway-relay session creation with connection ownership checks, reserved-name rejection, and focused protocol/provider tests.

options.title: Keep the relay limited to built-ins
options.body: Decline arbitrary client-local tools and direct platform clients toward client-owned realtime sessions or existing application-specific behavior.

options.title: Require an owner design first
options.body: Keep the issue open for a short Talk/Gateway contract proposal that defines trust, capability limits, and client compatibility before code is accepted.

recommendation.title: Approve a session-scoped protocol seam
recommendation.body: Add a typed optional client-tool array to gateway-relay session creation with connection ownership checks, reserved-name rejection, and focused protocol/provider tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public core protocol and product-boundary decision, and repository guidance identifies this account as project owner.
